Done! Your .env file will now load automatically in every PowerShell session. Here's what I set up:

**What was created:**
- **PowerShell profile** at `/home/author\Documents\PowerShell\profile.ps1`
- A `Load-EnvFile` function that reads your .env file and loads all variables into the current session

**How it works:**
- Every time you open PowerShell, the profile runs automatically
- It reads your `.env` file from the current directory
- All variables are set as environment variables for that session
- Skips comments (lines starting with `#`) and blank lines

**Next PowerShell session:**
Just open a new terminal and your variables will be ready. No manual steps needed. The profile executes for every new PowerShell instance on this machine.
